claims.claim: Optional Blackhole is missing as a plugin and deterministic engine.
claims.finding: Rust core compaction exists but no Blackhole implementation/native plugin was found; TypeScript package cannot be loaded by the native ABI.

claims.claim: Compiler normalizes messages into deterministic sections.
claims.finding: All normalized variants, source-index rules, sanitizer/filter and layout are specified, not only section names.

claims.claim: Compiler extracts goals/preferences/files/commits/outstanding/recent actions and builds a bounded brief.
claims.finding: Brief is bounded by line/content-word heuristics, not a global summary token budget. Findings and genuine user requests are also first-class sections. Exact limits and imperfect result/hash matching are specified.

claims.claim: Live-state reconstructs Active Goal, Mode And Plan, Background Shells and MCP/external use.
claims.finding: These are tolerant recorded-state projections, not runtime authority checks or live process polls.

claims.claim: Subagent digest reads latest child records.
claims.finding: Latest valid data is per child ID, but the last12 cap follows first-seen Map insertion order, not most recently updated child. Malformed later records can leave prior state.

claims.claim: tailBehavior supports ice-default/minimal with kept-tail and recall-noise handling.
claims.finding: Current code default is minimal, contradicting provenance prose. Minimal uses a missing cut-ID sentinel and does not insert a resume user message.

claims.claim: Checkpoint recall appends a fresh session-matching bounded Relevant Memory section.
claims.finding: It deletes a matching valid checkpoint before rendering, mismatched host IDs leave file, expiry15min, line cap24, and the nominal4000-unit header/body budget excludes an additional45-unit notice. No top-level JSON size/schema cap or atomic claim.

claims.claim: Refinement is optional, model-routed, bounded and falls back to deterministic text.
claims.finding: Recent serialized input is capped24000 UTF-16 units and completion maxTokens1200; the deterministic summary is not itself bounded. Requested300 words is not enforced. Output is explicitly unverified and structural neutralization is narrow.

claims.claim: Before-compaction hook can override core and kept-tool outputs are trimmed.
claims.finding: Exact gating, cancel/override result and context-only6000-unit text budget are specified.

claims.claim: Config at agentDir/ice-blackhole with enum/percent/refine/memory settings.
claims.finding: Exact default/precedence/write permission behavior specified, including unused memory flag and optional refineModel.

claims.claim: registerSettings and /blackhole provide status/percent/resume/pause/off.
claims.finding: Eight UI IDs and exact parser/preset/save behavior specified.

claims.claim: Mid-run compaction is missing in Rust; compaction exists mainly as manual flow.
claims.finding: Rust installs an AfterToolResults closure, checks threshold, compacts/persists and replaces context before the next model step. Blackhole-specific percent settings, pause/resume request protocol and suppression state remain absent.

claims.claim: TypeScript factories are not loaded by the native plugin model.
claims.finding: The current TS loader imports/caches factories while native loader accepts shared libraries through ice_plugin_register. Inline name/hidden/before-user semantics require a separate native application registration phase; launcher-specific feature implementations remain their area owners.

claims.claim: Plugin event coverage is already at parity because names exist in EventTag.
claims.finding: Enum coverage does not establish behavior. Native context/provider/input/message/tool hooks omit return transformations or fields, cancellation/error ordering differs, and ProjectTrust has no host emitter. Borrowed payload cleanup also has a concrete BeforeAgentStart mismatch.

claims.claim: Listed UI methods have no Rust equivalent.
claims.finding: Many exact controls are missing, but Rust already has owner-scoped text panels, queued editor text, structured dialogs and decoded Input handling. Widgets/footer/custom views/raw input are partial comparisons with explicit placement, ownership, payload, result and cancellation differences, not uniformly absent.

claims.claim: registerSettings has no native equivalent.
claims.finding: The TS group/items/onChange registry is real; the fully inspected native API/registry exposes no equivalent settings registrar. Native application settings alone do not provide extension-owned sections.

claims.claim: Introspection list includes missing getFlag and refreshToken host methods.
claims.finding: GetCliFlag is an implemented native action, though owner/absence semantics differ from TS getFlag. refreshToken is an OAuth ProviderConfig callback, not a public ExtensionAPI host method. Other listed context/tool/command metadata queries are separately missing or partial as specified.

claims.claim: Native tools/commands/flags/providers/dialog and specialized runtime actions are already implemented.
claims.finding: SDK registration, action dispatch, main-lane adapters and TUI dialog consumers are implemented. Existence of host action surfaces does not establish an external companion plugin or complete TS parity; child/stdio/side-question subsystem details remain their owners.

claims.claim: Current native entry symbol is ice_plugin_register.
claims.finding: The frozen loader/SDK require the ice_plugin_register symbol. No claim about availability of historical upstream binaries or releases is made from local source alone.

claims.claim: Custom entries must be added to the host API before later ports.
claims.finding: Native AppendEntry already handles customType/data and returns entryId. Missing pieces include the TypeScript durable option, GetSessionName/SetLabel, full entry rendering and exact metadata events. This narrows the required work.

claims.claim: ice-provider-settings supplies the provider submenu in /settings.
claims.finding: The factory registers providers settings at line 204 and captures the session context through session_start. Native generic TUI settings and catalog/scoped selectors exist but do not implement this provider catalog/refetch submenu.

claims.claim: The TS built-in provider registry has 41 providers; native built-ins are Anthropic and OpenAI.
claims.finding: all.ts registers 39 provider factories. OpenRouter image support is a separate capability, not an extra provider identity. Native core compiles Anthropic/OpenAI catalogs and supports configured/extension providers and three wire factories. Concrete external ice-package implementations were not inspected; core registration absence is not proof of package absence.

claims.claim: TS implements provider-specific PKCE/device OAuth; Rust delegates OAuth to provider plugins.
claims.finding: Seven concrete TS flows plus shared PKCE/device/callback helpers are specified. Native OAuth registration, begin/exchange/refresh/revoke dispatch, ABI ownership and CLI persistence are real. The inspected core has no equivalent concrete implementations of the seven flows; a TODO comment is not used to infer absence from external packages.

claims.claim: Radius gateway catalog refresh remains to be checked.
claims.finding: Radius normalizes gateway URLs, fetches/converts remote gateway catalog metadata and restores legacy OAuth gatewayConfig. Generic native provider config/package loading does not supply this concrete flow. The other listed AI utilities are owned by the AI audit.

claims.claim: refreshLocalModelsForStartup fetches the local endpoint catalog on launch unless offline.
claims.verdict: incorrect call behavior; split startup from explicit refresh
claims.finding: The frozen refreshLocalModelsForStartup body only loads the raw Omni/local credential and sets ICE_LOCAL_API_KEY. It neither fetches models nor consults the declared skip/refresh/onFailure options. Explicit refreshLocalModels performs /models fetch, validation, provider replacement and atomic-name rename; it returns updated:false on failure. AUTH-027 owns catalog row conversion.

claims.claim: Provider submenu and fast-route priority behavior are missing from Rust.
claims.verdict: provider submenu confirmed; fast-route metadata and shared option behavior separated
claims.finding: The submenu/refetch consumer is absent from the inspected native TUI. Omni catalog mapping marks eligible cx/gpt-5.6, cx/gpt-6-luna and cx/gpt-6-sol route families and honors serviceTiers, including an explicitly empty list. Shared fast option application and wire behavior are SET/SESSION/AI-owned; this entry does not infer them solely from catalog metadata.

claims.claim: ICE_LOCAL_BASE_URL, ICE_LOCAL_API_KEY and ICE_OMNI_BASE_URL are local-provider environment surfaces.
claims.verdict: confirmed with direction and precedence corrections
claims.finding: Base URL uses Omni then legacy-local nullish precedence then configured URL/default. ICE_LOCAL_API_KEY is assigned by credential startup and explicit refresh; the cited source does not read it there. ICE_AGENT_VIEW_COLORS is outside AUTH scope.

claims.claim: Rust lacks ultra and rejects an ultra thinkingLevelMap key; three private imported keys were remapped.
claims.verdict: source-level gap confirmed; private import counts unverified
claims.finding: TS declares off plus seven non-off levels through ultra, including the model-config schema. Native enum/map keys stop at max, so unknown ultra deserialization fails whole config. AI-005 owns runtime thinking/clamping. Actual user-directory imports and the stated three remappings cannot be checked under the explicit ban on real ~/.ice and ~/.icers reads.

claims.claim: Stored keys for zai/opencode/opencode-go/modal lack a native built-in catalog.
claims.verdict: public provider difference confirmed; Modal/private credential claim qualified
claims.finding: zai, opencode and opencode-go are actual TS built-in providers and absent from the native core's two compiled built-ins. Modal is not in the frozen TS 39-provider registry. Contents of private auth.json and whether any external provider package supplies these identities are explicitly unverified.

claims.claim: Rust model Bash lacks background and stdin parameters.
claims.finding: Model-facing Rust Bash is foreground-only. Rust interactive user Bash has an asynchronous task and cancellation slot, so background-like user execution must not be called wholly missing.

claims.claim: Automatic/manual release, a <=16 running registry, completion and cleanup.
claims.finding: Immediate explicit launches enforce 16 running shells; foreground adoption/release is not covered by that admission guard. Finished non-lingering retention is 20 in adoption order; lingering jobs remain. User-kill synthetic completion omits ordinary log/exit/lingering fields, and late settlement is ignored. Full-log creation/removal and process cleanup require distinct contracts.

claims.claim: bash_output/kill/input controls, waiting limits and input denied without UI.
claims.finding: Tool names and high-level limits are correct. No-UI denial applies to approval='ask'; allow bypasses confirmation. Exact wait/cursor/tail/grep, running-state checks, byte budgets and return schemas are specified in the entries.

claims.claim: Pattern/silence/interval watches, <=16 watches, <=10 fires and defaults.
claims.finding: Explicit create limits do not bound automatically installed default watches. Pattern defaults to one fire; other explicit watches default to three, with maximum ten. Explicit silence minimum is 5 seconds, while automatic silence settings follow their separate policy. Timed prompt detection, fire IDs, rearm/carry and cleanup are material omitted contracts; session owns alert delivery/wake.

claims.claim: Shells panel and RPC background controls/events.
claims.finding: The tool registry and session delivery contracts are documented in TOOLS and SESSION. RPC-026 verifies command responses and bash background/watch events. TUI-055 is a source-reviewed draft for the shells panel and must be published before global completion; no runtime behavior was exercised.

claims.claim: Output guard requires verification.
claims.finding: Rust already has a bounded 64-message RPC writer with ordered drain and failure cancellation. It lacks stdout isolation, individual/aggregate UTF-8 byte reservations, typed limit errors, transient 10 ms retries and guard lifecycle; print mode drops sink failures. Context breakdown and usage totals remain other-area claims.

notes: Claim metadata only; no detailed gap entry removed or rewritten. Canonical Blackhole first-pass records are eight; four additional-audit behaviors are retained outside the first-pass count.
